newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Argentina's Telecom feels recession - paper.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Telecom feels recession - paper.

text.p: Argentina's Telecom Argentina STET-France Telecom S.A. has seen profits drop by 25 percent over the last two years, a local financial newspaper reported.
Gazeta Mercantil said Telecom Argentina, which is owned by Italy's STET SpA and France Telecom, posted a $260 million profit in 1996. In 1994 the company reported a record $351 million net profit.
The paper quoted the company's International Manager Agustin Colombo Sierra as saying Telecom Argentina's bottom line has been hurt by the country's stubborn recession and high jobless rate.
"There is a permanent relationship between economic development and telephone demand, but we are going to try to recover revenues this year," he was quoted as saying.

To do that, the firm will try to offer more sophisticated services and invest in information technology, he said, according to the paper. The company also plans lay off workers, possibly cutting its workforce by another four percent, it said.
Gazeta did not say where Colombo Sierra spoke.

Telecom Argentina, which was privatized eight years ago, operates in the country's north. Spanish-owned Telefonica de Argentina, a unit of Telefonica de Espana, provides telecommunications services in the south.
